The republics in the Commonwealth of Nations are sovereign state members of the international organisation with a republican form of government. As of June 2022 [update] , 36 out of the 56 member states were republics. While King Charles III is the titular Head of the Commonwealth , he is not the head of state of the republican members. The King is, however, the reigning monarch in the Commonwealth realms . The Head of the Commonwealth role does not carry with it substantive power (what power it does have is probably exercisable by the Crown only on advice); instead, it is a symbol of the free association of Commonwealth members.
